title: Saved by Grace
alsoKnownAs: Some Day the Silver Cord Will Break
description: Saved by Grace in Tonic Solfa to SAVED BY GRACE: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the four verses and the refrain, and a piano.
about: Fanny Crosby wrote these words in 1891; some hymnals credit them to Ida Scott Taylor, one of her pen names. The tune is by George C. Stebbins (1894).
underlay: Some day the sil-ver cord will break, And I no more as now shall sing; But oh, the joy when I shall wake With-in the pal-ace of the King! And I shall see Him face to face, And tell the sto-ry— Saved by grace; And I shall see Him face to face, And tell the sto-ry— Saved by grace.

lines: Some day the silver cord will break,
And I no more as now shall sing;
But oh, the joy when I shall wake
Within the palace of the King!

verses.label: Refrain
lines: And I shall see Him face to face,
And tell the story—Saved by grace;
And I shall see Him face to face,
And tell the story—Saved by grace.
Some day my earthly house will fall.
I cannot tell how soon ’twill be;
But this I know—my All in All
Has now a place in Heav’n for me.
Some day, when fades the golden sun
Beneath the rosy tinted west,
My blessèd Lord will say, “Well done!”
And I shall enter into rest.
Some day: till then I’ll watch and wait,
My lamp all trimmed and burning bright,
That when my Savior opes the gate,
My soul to Him may take its flight.
